units: metres, three.js Y-up (glTF). Pedestal origin = centre of its bottom face, on the desk plane y = 0.

ring.note: position/quaternion already assume s01_scale. ring leans back-right resting on its lower edge (lowest vertex at top_y), opening toward camera-right, logo lower-left front (Figma 40004725:5602). Blender axis (-0.72, 0.5, -0.48), logo dir (-0.7, -0.55, -0.45)

filmOffset_or_viewOffset.note: Blender shift_y 0.135 of frame width moves the subject down. In three.js use camera.setViewOffset(fullW, fullH, 0, -0.135*fullW, fullW, fullH) or render to the photo aspect and match by eye.

camera.frame: photo 1818x1037, shown background-size: cover, centred (desktop 1440x900 crops the sides)

key.convention: three.js Y-up metres in pedestal space (= Blender (x, y, z) -> (x, z, -y)). Verified against the Cycles light: Blender key at (0.190, 0.120, 0.250) m aimed at (0, 0, 0.004); a Cycles SUN with this exact direction gives the same front-left shadow as the area light (renders/s01-pedestal/s01-key-area-vs-sun.png). Light travels (-0.570, -0.738, +0.360): left, down, toward the camera (+Z), so the ring shadow on the top runs LEFT-FRONT and is ~0.9 x the casting height long (elevation 47.6 deg).

shadow.note: Cycles area light D55 mm at 333 mm = 9.4 deg penumbra cone: contact-hard at the ring's touch point, ~3-4 mm soft at the shadow tip. With VSM (uniform blur) keep the blur small (~0.5 mm = 6 texels at 2048 over +-0.045 m) so the shadow stays clearly defined, as the user asked; do not raise radius to fake the tip softness.

fill.note: no front fill; keep key:fill high so the shadow on the top reads strong (Cycles key-only vs env-only: the env adds a soft overall lift, it does not cast the shaped shadow)

lights.environment: env/v2-env-paper.exr tinted warm (#FFB87A multiply), intensity ~0.28 for ring reflections

desk.note: transparent shadow catcher over the CSS photo; receives pedestal + ring shadows

proven: Blender Cycles renders in renders/s01-pedestal/ use exactly these values
proposed: three.js light/shadow numbers are a starting point; tune by eye against s01-pedestal-review-1440x900.png
